title: Transcriptomic Analyses Using R
author: Frank O Aylward
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.z3mf8k6

steps.title: Download and Prepare Data
steps.instruction: Clone the tutorial repository from GitHub and navigate into the directory.

substeps.instruction: Run `ls` to verify files 'homework_rnaseq_data.txt' and 'test_rnaseq_data.txt' are present

steps.title: Import Transcriptomic Data into R
steps.instruction: Load the transcriptomic data matrix into the R console, ensuring the full path to the file is provided.

substeps.instruction: Import the data using: `counts <- as.matrix(read.table("week11/transcriptomics_tutorial/test_rnaseq_data.txt", sep="\t", header=T, row.names=1))`

steps.title: Inspect Matrix Dimensions and Content
steps.instruction: Verify the size and initial entries of the loaded counts matrix.

substeps.instruction: View the first few lines using `head(counts)`

steps.title: Analyze Rank Abundance Distribution
steps.instruction: Calculate and visualize the abundance of genes ordered from most to least abundant.

substeps.instruction: Create a vector of summed abundance for all rows: `rankAbundance <- sort(rowSums(counts), decreasing=T)`

steps.title: Log-Transform the Data
steps.instruction: Apply a log10 transformation to the raw counts using a pseudocount of 1 to handle zero values.

substeps.instruction: Repeat the rank abundance analysis for the log-transformed data: `rankAbundance <- sort(rowSums(log), decreasing=T)`

steps.title: Generate Heatmaps
steps.instruction: Install necessary visualization packages and create heatmaps for both raw and log-transformed data.

substeps.instruction: Plot raw counts heatmap: `heatmap.2(counts, trace="none", col=palette)`

steps.title: Plot Individual Gene Expression
steps.instruction: Visualize the expression of a specific gene over time to identify patterns such as diel cycles.

substeps.instruction: Plot Gene1: `plot(counts["Gene1",], type="l", lwd=2, axes=F, xlab=NA)`
Add x-axis labels: `axis(1, at=c(1:25), colnames(counts), las=2)`
